cases.title: Shift reordering moves an item up the list and pushes the siblings it passed down one place each
Shift reordering moves an item down the list and pulls the siblings it passed up one place each
Shift reordering makes room for a create that lands on a position a sibling already holds
A gap already in the collection absorbs a shift rather than being pushed along ahead of it
Strict reordering, the default, still refuses a write onto a position a sibling holds
Shift reordering refuses a position below the declared minimum instead of arranging around it
A reorder that would displace a sibling the caller may not update is refused whole rather than applied in part
Compaction on delete renumbers the later siblings down so the collection stays contiguous
Compaction none, the default, leaves the hole a removal creates and moves nothing
A shift reorder queues the siblings it moved as ordinary update operations, so it replays with no new intent kind
